title: Cereal or Granola Bar with Non‑Chocolate Coating

content.title: About
content.content: A cereal or granola bar with a non‑chocolate coating is made from whole grains, nuts and dried fruit, covered with a thin layer of fruit‑based or yogurt glaze. It provides a quick snack, delivering energy and nutrients without cocoa.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bars often use whole rolled oats, which retain most of the fiber.
Non‑chocolate glazes can be made from berry purées, yogurt or honey, giving sweetness without caffeine.
These bars are popular with athletes because they are easy to digest and light on the stomach.
Many recipes add chia or flax seeds, rich in omega‑3 fatty acids.
Gluten‑free versions replace oats with quinoa or rice flakes.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole grains and dried fruit supply dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Oats and quinoa release glucose slowly, helping maintain steady energy levels.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Nuts and seeds provide monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The bar often contains vitamin E, magnesium and iron, which aid metabolic processes.

items.title: Lower added sugar
items.content: Non‑chocolate glazes are usually sweetened with honey or fruit purée, reducing refined sugar content.

items.title: Nut allergy
items.content: Bars may contain peanuts, almonds or other nuts that can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Even without chocolate, the bar is energy‑dense; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some versions use honey or fruit syrup, which may be a concern for people with diabetes.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: If wheat is used, the product is not suitable for those with celiac disease; look for a gluten‑free label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the bar straight from the wrapper as a quick snack, crumble it into yogurt or kefir, or slice it into oatmeal. It can be gently warmed to soften the glaze.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bars in a cool, dry place in their original packaging or an airtight container. For longer shelf life, keep them refrigerated to prevent glaze spoilage.
